newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal's inflation falls to 0.9 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Senegal's inflation falls to 0.9 pct in May.

text.p: Senegal's benchmark inflation index, measuring consumer price changes for an African family, dropped by 1.1 percent in May compared with April, bringing the annual inflation rate down to 0.9 percent from 2.5 percent.
The government is aiming to hold inflation to around 2.5 percent in the calendar year 1997.

The finance ministry said in a statement that food prices fell 1.6 percent in May from April. A five percent fall in the price of fish was by itself responsible for almost half the drop in the overall index in May.
Falling fish and meat prices over the past 12 months offset a sharp increase in the price of some other foodstuffs, such as sugar, the ministry said.
The index that measures a basket of European-style goods and services rose by 0.1 percent in May compared with April, when it rose by 0.9 percent.

Year-on-year European-style inflation was 2.0 percent in May, down from 2.4 percent in April. The increase in prices since the end of 1996 to end-May was 0.4 percent, as with the benchmark African index.
